about: Messages between Cuphead (client) and the ROUNDS card engine (server) over a localhost TCP socket, one JSON object per line. The engine writes its port to %LOCALAPPDATA%/CupRounds/engine.port once ROUNDS has loaded every card. Nothing from ROUNDS is written to disk here; images travel as base64 PNG in memory (the launcher's face pictures, content face_parts, come from a separate hidden ROUNDS run).

rows.response: cards[id, name, description, rarity, theme, colorHex, stats[text]]
stats (BuildStats), partial[] card names whose custom code does more than stats
color, shade, faceParts[png,x,y,w,h], gun png, bullet png, faceUnitsPerDiameter

rows.request: slot, vx, vy, height, ax, ay, grounded, shoot, block, hit, dead, fly (plane levels: hover in place, legs trailing)
rows.response: none (the engine moves that player's ROUNDS puppet)

rows.request: none (second localhost socket, port in frames.port)
rows.response: binary frames: int32 length, byte slot, uint16 width, uint16 height, RGBA pixels of the animated ROUNDS character
ok (ROUNDS gives that player every owned card it does not have yet, through ApplyCardStats)

rows.request: none (shared memory Local\CupRoundsArena3, ArenaLink.cs: control written by Cuphead every frame = camera, pause flag, Cuphead's sound-effects volume, per-player input (press counters), level colliders, events (damage, pit, spawn with a life number), pick requests, the plane hold: in a plane level ROUNDS's player is held at the plane's centre with no ROUNDS movement or gravity)
rows.response: result written by ROUNDS every frame = heartbeat first, players' position, velocity, health, block, dead, cards held and the last life number done (Cuphead ignores a slot until it matches), bullet hits on Cuphead targets, picked cards, plus the rendered ROUNDS layer in three frame buffers
ok, cardCount, ids[0] = JSON of the ROUNDS player's health, lifesteal, gun and movement stats and reward-card fields
